data.title: Confluence-level documentation as context — hypothesis review
body: # Confluence-level documentation as context — hypothesis review
- **Asked by:** the owner: *"if we integrate Confluence-level project documentation, the team and its agents get more context, and both work better."*

- **Constraints set by the owner during the review:** (1) no external links, documentation lives in the project repository; (2) documentation is not a note; (3) it must be quick and easy for an agent to read, and **not `.md` files**, which would break the concept of one journal.

- **Method:** `research-identify-assumptions` (10 assumptions, scored) · `research-pol-probe-advisor` (probe choice) · desk research with sources (a separate agent, 2026-09-18) · a measurement of this repository's own journal · the existing evidence in [Probe D](DOC-58), [context handoff](DOC-42) and [ADR-012](DOC-15)
- **Labels:** **Fact** (sourced or measured) · **Inference** · **Assumption**

- **Verdict:** **the value is not proven; the shape is now decided.** The owner's constraints ruled out every form except documentation as journal events, and the owner asked for it built. It is built as the smallest slice ([ADR-014](DOC-17), KAD-36…38). The three probes below decide whether anything more is built on it. The one defect found along the way is fixed (KAD-33).
## 1. What the hypothesis breaks into
"Confluence-level" can mean four different things. Only the last two are kadence's business:
| # | Meaning | Who already does it |
| a | A place where documents are written and versioned | git and Markdown. **Fact:** 70 Markdown documents in this repository |
| b | Pages, spaces, rendering, search, comments | Confluence, Notion, GitHub. Needs a server — out of bounds |
| c | **Knowing which document explains which work** | kadence since 0.4: `task doc` / `task doc add` ([Probe D](DOC-58): 34× less to read, upper bound) |
| d | **Getting that document to an agent without a search term** | kadence partly: `task show --json` returns `docs[]` |

After the owner's constraints, the hypothesis becomes: **documentation kept in the journal as its own entity, separate from notes, linked to the work and cheap for an agent to read, makes the team and its agents work better.** Parts (c) and (d) existed only for `.md` files, and the owner ruled those out. So the shape changes ([ADR-014](DOC-17)). The open question is still whether anyone writes documentation and whether it helps.
## 2. Evidence
### Ours, measured today

- **Fact.** This repository has 70 Markdown documents, 37 tasks, 13 decisions and 14 notes in its journal, and **0 `task.doc_linked` events**. The author built the linking feature and has not used it once in the four days of kadence running on kadence.

- **Fact.** A defect, found while checking how a wiki link would be handled: `task doc KAD-1 https://…` was recorded as `https:/…`, which is neither a URL nor a file, and it stays in an append-only journal permanently. `task doc add` also created a directory named `https:` in the repository. Fixed as KAD-33: a URL is refused, and the message points to a document in the repository.
### Outside, sourced

- **Fact.** Agents already read Confluence for free: Atlassian's Rovo MCP server has been GA since 2026-02-04, reads and writes pages, and lists Claude Code and Cursor as clients ([Atlassian](https://www.atlassian.com/blog/announcements/atlassian-rovo-mcp-ga), [docs](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/rovo-mcp/)).

- **Fact.** The only controlled study found (ETH Zurich, [arXiv 2602.11988](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11988), 138 + 300 tasks, Claude Code / Codex / Qwen Code): repository context files **did not generally raise success** and **raised inference cost by more than 20%**. Repository overviews did not help. Specific, non-standard instructions did.
- **Fact.** All 18 models tested got worse as input length grew ([Chroma, Context Rot](https://www.trychroma.com/research/context-rot)).

- **Fact.** Current documentation helps in a narrow case: supplying docs for an API released after the model's cutoff raised correct adoption from 74.6% to 92.9% ([arXiv 2604.09515](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.09515)).

- **Fact.** Stack Overflow 2025, professional developers: Confluence 36.5%, Markdown files 35.2%, Notion 17.2% ([SO 2025](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/technology)). More than 85% of Atlassian's cloud ARR comes from customers paying over $10k ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1650372/000165037226000031/teamq42026shareholderlet.htm)). No data was found for Ukraine or Poland.

- **Fact.** No git-native competitor (Beads, Backlog.md, Spec Kit, task-master) pulls wiki content in. The ones that integrate at all sync *tasks* with trackers. Swimm, the product that sold synced code documentation, pivoted to enterprise modernization.
### What this adds up to

- **Inference.** "More documentation → better agents" is contradicted by the only controlled evidence. What helps is **short, specific and current** documentation that arrives **when it is relevant**. That is (c)+(d) above, not a larger body of documents.

- **Inference.** Confluence-scale documentation is the kind the evidence says costs tokens and drifts. Our ICP of 3–8 developers is as likely to keep Markdown in the repo as to use Confluence, which fits the owner's constraint.
- **Inference.** Nobody in the category competes on documentation. That is either whitespace or a sign that nobody wants it, and zero links in our own journal points to the second.
## 3. Assumption map
`Risk = Impact × (1 − Confidence)`, with confidence low = 0.2 and medium = 0.5. All ten landed in **Test now**. Ordered:
| # | Assumption | Category | Risk | Evidence now |
| C1 | ICP teams keep enough project documentation for it to matter | value | 7.2 | not asked, Probe B branch 2 only asks where "why" lives |
| C2 | Agents do worse because a relevant repo document did not reach them | value | 7.2 | against in general (ETH); for, in the narrow "current, specific" case |
| C5 | kadence adds something the agent cannot get by reading `docs/` itself | strategy | 7.2 | Probe D: yes, as filtering; upper bound, questions chosen by the author |
| C8 | Documentation work does not push out outreach before Sep 22 / Oct 19 | team | 7.2 | **against**: 27 commits, 0 messages Sep 8–16 |
| C4 | People will link documents to work | usability | 6.4 | **against**: 0 links, even from the author |
| C3 | Documents in ICP repos are current enough that serving them helps | value | 5.6 | unknown; the drift argument is opinion only |
| C7 | A wiki layer in the repo is worth more than git + Markdown | strategy | 5.6 | against: nobody in the category, Swimm pivoted |
| C9 | Documentation-heavy teams are inside the ICP | gtm | 5.6 | partly: Confluence skews larger |
| C6 | Can be built with no network | feasibility | 4.0 | yes, after the owner's constraint |

| C10 | Nothing in a document needs erasing later | ethics | 5.6 | **changed by ADR-014**: the text now lives in an append-only journal. A pasted secret or a person's name can be removed only by rewriting git history. `doc edit` replaces what is shown, not what is kept, and the help has to say so |
## 4. Probes, cheapest first
The advisor's rule: the cheapest probe that tells the harshest truth. The riskiest assumptions are about value and usage, so no code is needed. Each probe below rides on work that is already planned.
| Probe | Tests | How | Pass | Fail → | By |

| **P1 · one question in Probe B** | C1, C2, C3 | Branch 2 gains one question: *"The last time an agent got something wrong that a document in your repo would have prevented — which document, and why didn't it read it?"* Asked only after the stories are told, never naming kadence | ≥ 2 of 5 give a dated story naming a document | 0 of 5 → documentation leaves the roadmap until an interviewee raises it | Oct 16 |

| **P2 · a third arm in Probe E** (KAD-10) | C2, C5 | The same five tasks: nothing / journal / **journal + the linked document**. Count clarifying questions and tokens to the first correct step | the document arm cuts questions or tokens by ≥ 20% on ≥ 3 of 5 tasks | no gain → the ETH result holds here too; `docs[]` stays as it is | with KAD-10 |

| **P3 · dogfood** (with KAD-3) | C4 | For two weeks, every task in this repository that has a design document gets `task doc`. Count `task.doc_linked` events, and note every time linking felt pointless | ≥ 5 links made without a reminder | < 5 → linking is a feature nobody reaches for, which is a note, not a roadmap item | Oct 2 |
## 5. What was built — 2026-09-18, the smallest slice
Designed with `eng-api-and-interface-design`, recorded in ADR-014 and DEC-14, built test-first:
| Piece | What it does | Why this shape |

| `doc.written` event | one whole revision: `title`, `body`, `parents` | parents turn two concurrent edits into a **visible conflict**, not a silent loss (I1). The body is stored as lines, so `git diff` stays readable |
| `doc.linked` event | a document explains a task | additive and conflict-free. Links to deleted tasks are dropped, the same rule notes follow |
| `kadence doc add / edit / show / list / link` | write and read, all with `--json` | text from `--body`, `--file` or `--stdin`. **No `.md` file is created** |
| `doc list`, `task show` | titles and `bytes`, **never bodies** | the agent decides from the size whether to read. The index costs nothing |
| `prime` | names the documentation of the work you claimed, at most 3 | the one place a document reaches the agent without a search term |
| warning past 16 KiB | written, with a warning | the evidence says long documents hurt. Splitting is the author's call |

Verified: 1046 tests. A 64 KiB body and a revision history past 128 KiB go through a real process and a pipe intact. `prime` stays within 40 lines and 3 KiB. Timing is about +4% on 10 000 events with 2 MB of documentation.
## 6. Decision gate — Oct 19, with the Probe B verdict
| Result | Then |
| P1 **and** P2 pass, **and** ≥ 5 documents written through `kadence doc` in this repository | Next slice: `$EDITOR` for people (KAD-39), `decision add --doc DOC-N` |
| One passes | Nothing more is built. The commands stay |
| Neither passes | The commands stay, documented as an experiment that did not pull. The finding goes into the verdict |
## 7. Rejected, and why
| Option | Reason |

| A Confluence connector (read or sync) | Atlassian gives it away as MCP. It would be a second network package, which [ADR-012](DOC-15) says needs its own decision. The owner declined external links |
| URL links in `task doc` | The owner's constraint. Also: kadence could never tell whether the page still exists |
| `.md` files that kadence creates and indexes | The owner's constraint: a second store beside the journal. A merge of one file is a text conflict, which is our competitors' failure |
| A wiki layer (spaces, rendering, search) | That is a different product. No competitor in the category does it, and the evidence says a larger body of documentation does not help agents |
## What this review did not answer
Whether the owner's own experience of agents missing documentation is common. It is the most likely source of the hypothesis, and it is exactly what P1 asks strangers. Until then it is n = 1.
